questions.stem: How many main energy stores are there in the modern physics model?
questions.explanation: There are eight main energy stores: kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, thermal, chemical, nuclear, electrostatic, and magnetic.

questions.stem: Which energy store is associated with a moving object?
questions.explanation: The kinetic energy store holds energy due to an object's motion. Any moving object with mass has energy in its kinetic energy store.

questions.stem: A book on a high shelf has energy in which store?
questions.explanation: An object raised above the ground has energy in its gravitational potential energy store, which depends on mass, height, and gravitational field strength.

questions.stem: Food, batteries, and fossil fuels store energy in which energy store?
questions.explanation: Food, batteries, and fossil fuels all store energy in chemical bonds. This energy is released during chemical reactions.

questions.stem: What is the SI unit of energy?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of energy is the joule (J). Energy in all stores is measured in joules.

questions.stem: Which energy store is associated with a stretched spring?
questions.explanation: A stretched or compressed spring stores energy in its elastic potential energy store. This energy is released when the spring returns to its natural shape.

questions.stem: The thermal energy store of an object is related to:

options.text: The temperature and internal energy of the object
The chemical composition of the object

questions.explanation: The thermal energy store depends on the temperature and internal energy of an object. Hotter objects have more energy in their thermal energy store.
